newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan low long-term rates reflect uncertainty - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan low long-term rates reflect uncertainty - BOJ.

text.p: Current low long-term interest rates in Japan may reflect market uncertainty about the economy and a technical factor in markets ahead of book-closings for the financial year at the end of March, a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said on Tuesday.
Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, told reporters that the market does not always move in line with economic fundamentals.
There is a theory that long-term interest rates move on expectations regarding inflation, and that theory may be confirmed when the movements of the rates are observed over the long term, he said.
"We may need more time to assess the basic trend of long-term interest rates."
Matsushima said the impact on consumption of a planned rise in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1 may be relatively mild.
Compared with 1989, when the consumption tax was introduced, consumers are more cautious now about spending money ahead of the implementation of the higher tax, he said.

In particular, consumers were not rushing to buy general goods sold at supermarkets and department stores, though there were some movements in advanced purchases of high-priced items such as houses and cars.
